findings.title: The rot named limit names only requirement citations; ruling and goal citations can rot the same way
findings.recommendation: The new paragraph says every row except decision applies to a carried citation as to a new one, and the named limit then names only the requirement case. A carried ruling or goal citation is refused the same way when an architect session drops or renumbers the cited ID in the doc's Rulings index or Goals (checkCitationExists' ruling and goal cases re-run rulingExists/goalExists on a replacement). Either widen the named limit to say a carried requirement, ruling or goal citation is checked as a new one is (D-rl-2's reasoning covers all three), or add a clause saying why rulings and goals cannot lose an ID. explore.md's Domain table marks both rows 'unchanged' without the caveat it gives the requirement row.

findings.title: The generated reference's carried exception is checked by eye only
findings.recommendation: proposal.md's fifth What Changes bullet and task 1.2 put the carried exception into CITATION_EXISTS.decision, but no scenario covers it and task 2.4 only confirms the generated decision-records.md by inspection. test/core/decision-writing-parity.test.ts already checks DECISION_RECORDS_REFERENCE (citationFailure checks only that each kind is named), so a reverted line would pass every test. If it matters, add one assertion there that the decision line names the carried case; otherwise leave the manual confirmation as it stands.

stale_suppressed.title: The two predicates may disagree on duplicate IDs
stale_suppressed.evidence: src/core/parsers/explore-rules.ts:381-391 (liveDecisionIds) and :410-415 (decisionEntryText) both take the first Decisions entry that carries an ID, through the same collectSections and readDecision

commentary: Small, well-sourced change. I checked the design's claims against the code: checkReplaces runs before checkCitationExists and holds relies_on equal to the original's (REPLACEMENT_LINK_FIELDS.ledger), the carried flag already exists in checkDecisionLinks, and the brief's decision case calls decisionEntryText, so the gate and the reader end up on one predicate. Case 1 holds: the archived seam-chaining explore.md carries D-sc-9 with 'Disposition: assigned driver', and both ledger files it names exist. The safety argument (a carried citation was live once) holds through chains, because each link's relies_on equals the root's. orbit validate passes; the two new scenarios are undeclared until tasks 2.1 and 2.2 declare them, as expected before apply. Both findings are about how complete the stated limits and checks are, not about the mechanism.

direction.reasoning: The mechanism is correct and minimal. It reuses the brief's own predicate behind a flag that already exists, and the code confirms the safety argument. What is left is optional wording about which carried citations can still rot and an optional assertion on the generated reference. Neither changes what apply would build, so the change can go to apply after a short walk.
